chapter: Heroes, heard bands and Lunceford's life on the road
title: Henry Clay, the trumpeter who made him carry his drums home
summary: Crawford recalls the trumpet player Henry Clay, who owned the only car and made him walk a mile home with his drums.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Now, this is -- this, what we're talking about now is this trumpet player, Henry Clay, who was with the band.
That guy used to -- he was the only one had a car, and after a gig he would make me -- drive me by his house, which was a mile from my house, and make me haul -- he was afraid to go in his garage.

He was just a -- well, he was just mama and daddy boy. His father gave him everything he wanted, and he would make me go by his house, take my drums out, bass drum and all, my satchel or whatever I could afford to carry my other traps in, make me walk a mile home, 2:00, 3:00 4:00 o'clock in the morning, because he was afraid to go in his garage. I'll never forget it. And that's that.
